title: STAPLING INSTRUCTIONS
summary: General stapling (stitching) rules for attaching rubber to metal anywhere on the car: how much staple wire to feed per stitch based on crown size and work thickness, with sketches of 37 1/2 degree, 45 degree and flat clinches. No specific parts.
notes: WIRE DRAW = 2C + 2T (Figure 1, crown sizes .175 through .50: clinched legs should just about meet).
WIRE DRAW = C + 2T + 3/8" (Figure 2, crown sizes over .50: each clinched leg 3/16" long).
C = CROWN SIZE, T = THICKNESS OF WORK.
Examples given: 7/16" crown, 3/16" work -> 1-1/4" wire draw; 1-1/8" crown, 1/2" work -> 2-1/2" wire draw.
Formulas don't account for material type; some materials may need different leg lengths, but use Fig. 1 for crowns .175-.50 and Fig. 2 above .50 as a general rule.
NOTE: Staples must not be countersunk in the rubber more than twice the diameter of the staple wire, to avoid tearing the rubber.
